newsitem.title: USA: Mattel to merge with Tyco Toys.
newsitem.headline: Mattel to merge with Tyco Toys.

text.p: Mattel Inc and Tyco Toys Inc said on Monday they would merge in a stock transaction valued at $755 million.
Under the agreement, Tyco shareholders will receive Mattel stock worth $12.50 for each Tyco share.
On Friday Mattel shares closed at 30-5/8 and Tyco at seven. Based on Friday's closing prices, the deal represents a 78 percent premium for Tyco shareholders, the companies said.
They said the merger is expected to be completed in the first half of 1997. If so, it is expected to be accretive to earnings per share in the first year, they said.
The boards of both companies have approved the merger.
"The outstanding worldwide potential for Tyco's well-known brands will be fully realized through this merger with Mattel," Mattel Chairman John Amerman said in a statement.
The companies said the merger would provide synergies resulting from the integration of their manufacturing and international distribution networks, and this would provide significant cost savings.

Mattel Chief Operating Officer Jill Barad said Tyco's time-tested brands will mesh well with Mattel's four major core brands -- Barbie, Hot Wheels, Disney and Fisher Price. She said Tyco's international core brand sales are less than 25 percent of its overall business, and with Mattel's extensive distribution network, the merger provides an excellent opportunity for growth.
In February Mattel withdrew its $52 per share offer to buy Hasbro, which objected to the deal on antitrust grounds.
